newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq asks U.N. to release $50 million for haj.
newsitem.headline: Iraq asks U.N. to release $50 million for haj.

text.p: Iraq has asked the United Nations to release $50 million of its money frozen in Arab banks to enable Iraqis to perform this year's pilgrimage to Mecca, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Tuesday.

INA said Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf sent a message to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan demanding that the world body also allow Iraq to use civil planes to transport its pilgrims to Mecca.

"Iraq has called on the U.N. secretary-general to support its demand for the freeing of $50 million of its assets frozen at a number of Arab banks to secure needs of Iraqi pilgrims for hard cash for the next haj season," INA said.
"In his message, Sahaf also called on Annan to use his good offices at the U.N. Security Council to agree to flights by Iraqi Airways to carry pilgrims from Baghdad to Mecca," INA said.
The United Nations imposed a trade and air embargo on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Iraq said this month seven Arab countries owed it about $1.4 billion. A finance ministry source said they were Saudi Arabia, Syria, Bahrain, Kuwait, Somalia, the United Arab Emirates and Egypt.
Last time Iraq sent its pilgrims to Mecca was in 1992 when about 11,000 Iraqis travelled to the holy city by land.
